site.name: BSF Indoors
site.tagline: Year-round black soldier fly farming, no greenhouse required
site.description: Firsthand guides, gear reviews, and breeding protocols for keeping a self-sustaining black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) colony indoors — including indoor mating, lighting, prepupae self-harvest, and feedstock troubleshooting.

region._agentNote: BSF farming itself is climate-controlled, so 'region' here refers to the cold-climate audience for whom indoor operation is the differentiator. Cache Valley operator; addresses readers in any climate where outdoor BSF is impractical.
region.name: Cache Valley, Utah
region.climateZone: USDA 5b, semi-arid, ~4,500 ft elevation, long cold winters

audience.primary: Backyard/homestead operators in cold climates who want a year-round BSFL colony for chicken/fish feed, composting, and frass — without an outdoor or greenhouse setup
audience.secondary: Aquaponics hobbyists, vermiculture overlap audiences, off-grid and food-resilience readers, small-scale alternative-protein curious

theme._agentNote: BSF visual cues: dark iridescent blue-black adults, warm decomposition browns, frass amber. Avoid the worm-farm green palette; this niche is closer to entomology/lab aesthetic than to garden aesthetic.
